server.instructions:
CandleStack is a lab for experiments on financial time series: a user uploads a trading model (Keras or ONNX), describes its input in a manifest and backtests it on market data, crypto from Binance and US stocks from Alpaca, then compares the results and publishes the good ones.

You act as the user who signed you in, with an API key or by allowing you on CandleStack (OAuth). The scopes of that sign-in decide which tools work: read (everything that only reads), backtests, models and publish. Call get_me first to see who you act for and what you may do. A tool that changes data says so in its annotations.

A failed tool call answers a problem as JSON: its type (https://candlestack.tech/problems/<slug>) names what went wrong and its detail says what to do.

Docs for agents: https://candlestack.tech/docs/agents/ and for this server: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/. The resource candlestack://docs lists every docs page and reference.

tools.description:
Who you act for: the CandleStack user who signed you in (an API key or OAuth), and the scopes of that sign-in, which decide the tools you may call. Call it first to check the connection, and when a tool answers the problem missing-scope.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#get_me

Scope.description:
What an API key may do. `read`: every GET; `backtests`: start, rename and star
backtests; `models`: upload models, add their manifests, rename, star and delete them;
`publish`: publish and unpublish backtests. Managing keys, deleting the account, sign-in
methods and signing out need the browser session whatever the scopes.
Scope.title: Scope

tools.description:
Checks a sweep without starting anything: every combination of `base` (the setup of one backtest: model, data, decision, execution, benchmarks) and the values in `vary` (models, instruments, periods, decision rules) passes the checks of a new backtest, and the user's queue has room for all of them. Use it before run_sweep to see how many backtests a grid makes and what each one runs.

Answers the count, the limit of 20, the queue's room and each setup in the grid's order. A setup that fails a check is the problem of that check with `setup`, its place from 1.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#validate_sweep

tools.title: Check a sweep

tools.description:
Starts a backtest for every combination of `base` (the setup of one backtest) and the values in `vary`: models (each model's manifest sets what it reads and its timeframe, so list models to vary those), instruments, periods and decision rules, 2 to 20 backtests. All go to the end of the user's queue, which runs one at a time, or none does. `metric` is the statistic the ranking orders by.

Answers the sweep: its ID, each backtest's ID, status and setup, and the progress. Follow it with get_sweep until `done`. The backtests are ordinary ones, with the sweep's ID.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#run_sweep

tools.title: Run a sweep

tools.description:
A sweep of the user: how many of its backtests are queued, running, finished and failed, each backtest's ID, status and setup, and once none is queued or running (`done`) the ranking, best first, by `metric` or else the sweep's own. Values that read the same in the app share a rank, and the best and the worst are marked as the Compare page marks them.

Call it again while it runs; a backtest takes a minute or a few. For every statistic of the backtests, compare them with their IDs.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#get_sweep
